Faculty Mentor: Dr. Shane McCarty

Applied logistic regression modeling in R to investigate whether promotion and prevention mindsets predict health- and safety-related goal preferences.

Served as first author on a poster abstract accepted by the 2026 American Public Health Association Annual Meeting.

Conduct ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis tests, logistic regression, and machine-learning classifiers; manuscript in preparation.

Faculty Mentor: Dr. Shane McCarty

Collaborated with a seven-person team to research the impact of endometriosis on women’s mental health, culminating in two poster presentations to peers and faculty in December 2023 and 2024.
Conducted quantitative data analysis using SPSS for six or more hours weekly, collaborating with peers to develop studies on vaccine hesitancy among pregnant women.
Designed and distributed a comprehensive campus-wide survey using Qualtrics, collecting and analyzing responses.

January 2026–May 2026 Histopathology Thyroid Cancer Detection Using YOLO — Group Project, Binghamton University

Built a YOLO-based deep-learning model to detect thyroid cancer, abnormal, and normal tissue in histopathological images for potential pre-screening applications.
Evaluated model performance through Type I and Type II error analysis, assessing risks of missed diagnoses and unnecessary follow-up.
Interpreted confusion matrices to assess model limitations related to class imbalance and dataset representativeness.



September 2025–December 2025 Deep Reinforcement Learning in Board Games — Group Project, Binghamton University

Implemented deep reinforcement-learning agents in PyTorch to play Tic-Tac-Toe and Connect Four through self-play.
Designed neural networks mapping board states to action values and visualized training performance using Matplotlib.
